scope: Deep audit only; no model retraining, active-prediction change, Optuna run or tournament-engine promotion.

executive_verdict.priority: Fix rules and data semantics, then unify around the strongest historically validated match model before adding complexity.

current_algorithm.match_cache: One fixed prediction matrix per team pair and stage reused across all tournaments.
current_algorithm.group_match_model: Independent Poisson score matrix using current external Elo plus exponentially decayed goals-for/goals-against profiles.
current_algorithm.knockout_match_model: Bernoulli advancement draw from 90-minute win probability plus draw probability allocated by Elo expected score.
current_algorithm.penalty_shootout: Not simulated; included implicitly in Elo allocation of a 90-minute draw.
current_algorithm.group_ranking: Points, goal difference, goals scored, then random tie-break.
current_algorithm.best_thirds: Points, goal difference and goals scored; remaining ties inherit input order.
current_algorithm.central_scenario: Selected from persisted complete paths; only 100 of 50,000 complete paths are retained.

strengths: Every run is a complete end-to-end tournament and finished official results are locked.
Group score sampling and standings are connected; knockout winners propagate coherently.
The direct match model does not reuse qualification probability as head-to-head strength.
The fixed seed makes runs reproducible.
50,000 runs give a worst-case Monte Carlo 95% sampling margin of about 0.44 percentage points.

weaknesses.issue: The official 2026 bracket rules are not encoded; teams are dynamically seeded by Elo.
weaknesses.impact: Opponent paths and title probabilities are structurally wrong even if match probabilities were perfect.

weaknesses.issue: The tournament uses V3 instead of the project's stronger historically validated quant_hybrid_v2.2 match probabilities.
weaknesses.impact: The simulator repeats a weaker predictive model 50,000 times.

weaknesses.issue: Extra time and penalties are not simulated as separate processes.
weaknesses.impact: Knockout advancement probabilities and explanations are simplified and not empirically validated.

weaknesses.issue: Group tie-break rules stop after points, goal difference and goals scored.
weaknesses.impact: Head-to-head criteria are skipped and unresolved ties become random; qualification boundaries were affected in the persisted sample.

weaknesses.issue: AET/PEN historical score semantics are unresolved.
weaknesses.impact: Ninety-minute goal profiles and backtests may contain extra-time or shootout-contaminated outcomes.

weaknesses.issue: All tournaments condition on one fixed parameter estimate and independent match draws.
weaknesses.impact: Model uncertainty and correlated tournament form are understated.

weaknesses.issue: Only the first 100 complete paths are persisted for central-scenario selection.
weaknesses.impact: Central-scenario selection has a worst-case 95% sampling margin near 9.8 percentage points.

weaknesses.issue: Static current external Elo is used for forecasts and coverage is incomplete.
weaknesses.impact: Six tournament teams fall back to 1500 and one lacks a historical profile.

weaknesses.issue: The same match process is used for groups and knockout.
weaknesses.impact: Stage-specific tactics and draw behavior are not learned.

weaknesses.issue: No tournament-level historical replay validates group ranks, best thirds, bracket paths or title calibration.
weaknesses.impact: Good single-match metrics do not prove good tournament probabilities.

applicable_methods.method: Reusable quant_hybrid_v2.2 inference bundle plus calibrated score reconstruction
applicable_methods.reason: It already materially outperforms V3 out of sample; model/state persistence is the missing engineering layer.

applicable_methods.method: Exact FIFA rules engine and official Annex C bracket mapping
applicable_methods.reason: This is deterministic rules data, not a predictive-data limitation.

applicable_methods.method: Chronological regulation-time data cleanup and stage-segmented replay
applicable_methods.reason: Dates, stages and source statuses already exist.

applicable_methods.method: Hierarchical/weighted Poisson with shrinkage and internal ratings
applicable_methods.reason: Useful for score matrices and low-sample teams; must beat the active baseline out of sample.
Technically feasible, but prior local Dixon-Coles tests did not pass promotion guards.

applicable_methods.method: Separate extra-time intensity and conservative penalty baseline
applicable_methods.reason: AET/PEN rows exist, but sample size requires shrinkage; penalties should remain near 50/50 unless validated.

applicable_methods.method: Bootstrap/model ensemble and per-tournament latent form shock
applicable_methods.reason: Can represent parameter uncertainty and correlated performance using existing historical scores.

applicable_methods.method: Player, injury, lineup, odds and broad xG models
applicable_methods.reason: Coverage is absent or too sparse; adding them now would create unreliable complexity.

target_architecture: Data contract: regulation-time scores, extra-time scores, shootout winner, neutral context, stage, official rules and identities.
Reusable pre-match inference bundle: chronological internal rating, team history, quant_hybrid probabilities and calibrated score distribution for arbitrary pairings.
Stage-aware match layer: group 90-minute score model; knockout 90-minute score model; extra-time model; penalty model.
Exact tournament rules engine: complete tie-break hierarchy, best-third ranking and official 2026 bracket mapping.
Uncertainty-aware Monte Carlo: multi-seed convergence, bootstrap/model ensemble and optional calibrated tournament-form latent effects.
Streaming aggregation: retain marginals plus a broad reservoir/top-K of complete paths rather than only the first 100.
Scenario selection: choose a coherent medoid/representative path from all retained candidates using event likelihood and distribution distance.
Tournament-level validation: historical replay of complete tournaments with proper scoring, calibration curves and rule correctness tests.

delivery_plan.outcome: Use the strongest validated project model for every possible matchup.
tasks: Calibrate group and knockout segments separately

delivery_plan.outcome: Model how knockout matches actually finish.
tasks: Simulate 90 minutes, extra time and penalties separately
Use conservative shrinkage for small AET/PEN samples

delivery_plan.outcome: Prove tournament probabilities, not only match probabilities.
tasks: Replay historical tournaments end to end
Measure group-rank, qualification, stage-reach and champion calibration

research_references.topic: World Cup simulation with Elo-Poisson and Monte Carlo
Dixon-Coles extensions and dependent score models
Probabilistic football model comparison and calibration
IFAB outcome, extra time and penalty-shootout rules

recommendation: Do not build a V4 by adding ad-hoc signals. Build a rules-correct V3.5 around a reusable quant_hybrid inference contract, explicit knockout processes and tournament-level validation; promote only if it beats V3 and the active match baseline out of sample.
